generatedFrom: 2026-09-13. Every ceiling re-cut with a 250-byte tolerance over the larger of the local and CI measurement, and the reason is a mistake worth recording: the 2026-09-12 pass ratcheted each ceiling to the exact byte a local build produced, with the note that no headroom was banked. CI then failed five routes by 13 to 58 bytes, and a second local build moved the shared chunk by 1 — gzip output is not byte-stable across builds or machines, so a zero-slack ceiling is a guaranteed red build rather than a strict one. 250 bytes is about 0.2% and still leaves every route far below where it started this week (students 142600 -> 138241, defaulters 145300 -> 136138, transactions 151000 -> 142656). The rule is unchanged: ceilings ratchet down. They just cannot be cut finer than the build is repeatable.
